title: Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
key_facts: Character.AI, which lets users create AI characters and chat with them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following lawsuits and struggles to scale; a court document puts assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.
It agreed to sell some assets to Disney for $20 million plus a non-exclusive perpetual licence to its technology.

CEO Colin Adams says the company keeps operating during a court-supervised sale process expected to close in late November or early December; there is no bid or buyer yet and the platform will be wound down if no workable bid comes.
Former Character.AI employees joined Disney last month with former CEO Karandeep Singh Anand and provide transition services.

Founded in late 2021 by Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas; reached unicorn status in September 2022 on a $150 million raise; Google struck a $2.7 billion licensing deal in August 2024 and both founders returned to Google.

It faced lawsuits, including one after the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother says he became obsessed with a chatbot, and a Texas investigation; it settled some suits and banned minors.
TechCrunch reads the filing as showing consumer AI products are hard to scale and monetise, because costs rise with use; Character.AI had raised over $193 million, per PitchBook.
quote_evidence: Only five years into its journey, Character.AI, which lets users create AI characters and have conversations with them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following a slew of lawsuits and struggles to scale its popular platform.
The startup has also agreed to sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million, as well as a non-exclusive perpetual license for its technology.
However, he did note that there isn't yet a bid for the company's assets or a buyer.
why_it_matters_hint: A once-popular consumer AI chat platform may be sold or shut down within weeks, and TechCrunch sees it as a sign of how hard consumer AI is to make pay.
